title: Real Estate Broker Commission in India: Rates, Who Pays, RERA, GST and TDS
seoTitle: Real Estate Broker Commission Rates in India: Who Pays
excerpt: Broker commission rates in India: no fixed national rate, who pays in resale vs new projects, Haryana's 1% cap, CP payouts, RERA, 18% GST and 2% TDS.

faqs.question: How much commission does a real estate broker charge in India?
faqs.answer: There is no national fixed rate. In resale and rentals the fee is agreed in writing between the broker and the buyer, seller or tenant, usually as a percentage of the price or a share of the rent. In new projects the developer pays the channel partner under its CP agreement. Haryana is an exception: its property dealer rules allow 1% of the agreed price, half from each side.

faqs.question: Who pays the broker commission on a new project flat?
faqs.answer: Normally the developer. Channel partners are paid by the developer under their CP agreement, so a home buyer booking a new-project flat through a CP usually pays no brokerage. If a CP asks you for brokerage on a new booking, ask for the reason in writing.

faqs.question: Does RERA fix broker commission?
faqs.answer: No. The RERA Act, 2016 does not set commission rates. It requires agents to register with the state RERA authority (Section 9), sets their duties (Section 10) and penalises breaches with up to ₹10,000 a day, up to 5% of the property's cost (Section 62).

faqs.question: Is there a legal cap on brokerage in Haryana?
faqs.answer: Yes. Rule 10 of the Haryana Regulation of Property Dealers and Consultants Rules, 2009 allows 1% of the agreed consideration value, paid half by the seller and half by the buyer. HRERA said in October 2020 it would enforce the cap. Check the current position with HRERA before agreeing a fee.

faqs.question: Is GST charged on real estate brokerage?
faqs.answer: Yes. Brokerage is a taxable service at 18% GST. A broker must register for GST once yearly turnover crosses ₹20 lakh for services in most states (₹10 lakh in special category states) and then adds GST to the invoice.

faqs.question: What is the TDS rate on brokerage and commission?
faqs.answer: 2% once commission paid to one person crosses ₹20,000 in the year, or 20% without a PAN. From 1 April 2026 this rule sits in Section 393(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, which replaced Section 194H of the 1961 Act. Confirm the current rate with your chartered accountant.

faqs.question: What is a 70/30 commission split?
faqs.answer: It is how a brokerage firm and its agent share a commission: the agent keeps 70% and the firm keeps 30% for office, leads, software and support. The term comes mainly from the US; in India firms use many models, from salary plus incentive to a share of each deal.

faqs.question: When does a developer pay a channel partner?
faqs.answer: At the milestone written in the CP agreement, for example after the buyer has paid a set share of the price or after the agreement for sale is registered. The agreement should also say how buyers are registered to a CP and what happens to commission if a booking is cancelled.
